Subject: RE: Novus eval — token assumptions & quick ops levers

Camila — quick read and numbers below. High-level: assumptions are conservative but we can present a few optimizations to Procurement that materially reduce unit cost if Novus is willing to accept minor tradeoffs.

Key econ inputs (summary):
- Baseline tokens/month: 3.6B (10k DAU, median 370 tokens/session)
- Hosted price (current recommended model mix): $12 per 1M generated tokens, $7 per 1M prompt tokens (blended ~ $10/1M tokens when weighted) — see csv for model split
- Caching: 30% effective hit lowers generated tokens by ~22% (because some prompts are still unique), net tokens/month -> ~2.8B
- Batching: for interactive endpoints we target latency SLO; batching to average size 8 gives ~12–18% token cost savings due to better packing and fewer model calls; larger batches (16+) are better for throughput but risk pushing 95pctl latency over 450ms in our tests.
- Prefetching KB answers (for known flows) can add compute but overall reduces total generator tokens by up to 10% for flows with repetitive queries.

Net effect examples (rounded):
- Conservative (no caching, minimal batching): cost ~ $36k / month (3.6B tokens @ $10/1M)
- With caching (30%) + moderate batching: cost ~ $28k / month
- Aggressive ops (prefetch + 40% cache + batching 12): cost ~ $23k / month

Risks/notes to call out on MAP:
- If real user behavior skews to longer sessions (e.g., >700 tokens/session), costs scale linearly — include 2x stress case in the MAP.
- Embedding costs: plan for 2 models — dense embeddings for semantic search (higher perf) and a lower-cost variant for large-scale vectorization. We’ve included both in the csv so Procurement can see the delta.

Ops levers to propose on the MAP:
- Default prompt templates to cap generation tokens where acceptable
- Cache TTL and prefix caching for KB queries (we recommend 24–48h TTL for FAQs in pilot)
- Batching profile: interactive route with batch target 8, bulk ingestion route with batch 64+ and different SLOs

I attached token-assumptions-20250424.csv with the line items. I can write a one-paragraph econ summary for Procurement if you want to include it in the MAP.

-ben
